# IONOS Image Style Guidelines

Source: UDS Image Generation Service rules

## Overall Tone

Professional, trustworthy, optimistic, modern. Warm approachability — not cold or corporate. People look confident and capable. Environments feel lived-in, real, and inviting. Bright, airy, and uplifting — never dark, moody, or dramatically shadowed.

## Image Types

Identify the correct type before generating. If ambiguous, prefer portrait for person-focused briefs, scenario for product-focused briefs.

| Type | Use when | Key framing rule |
|------|----------|-----------------|
| avatar | Square (1:1) crop for profile/card use. Face is focal point. | Face 100% visible — full forehead to chin, no cropping. Vary shot distance and camera angle across generations. Do not specify lighting or camera equipment. |
| person-scenario | Subject is mid-action in their environment; what they are doing tells the story. | Long shot (full body head-to-floor) is the default. Face 100% visible. Subject engaged mid-action, never posed. Waist shot only if context still shows. No symmetrical framing, no plain backdrop. |
| portrait | Subject faces the camera in a professional or personal environment; identity and context tell the story. | State face anchor first in every prompt. Framing must be stated positively (see Face and Body Framing Rule). Component-side placement rule applies. |
| scenario | Product, device, or digital interaction is the focal point; people are secondary or partial. | Screen/device is the hero. People cropped, blurred, or backgrounded — face must NOT be visible and in focus. Depth of field sharpens the product interaction. |

## Portrait: Component-Side Placement

When the brief names a UI component AND specifies a side (left/right):
- Left: subject anchored in the left third, body and gaze angled slightly right toward the text column
- Right: subject anchored in the right third, body and gaze angled slightly left toward the text column

State this explicitly in the prompt: "person standing in the left third of the frame, body and gaze angled slightly to the right."

## Module Bias

The named UI module biases scale/framing. Module fills what the brief leaves open — never overrides explicit brief settings.

| Module | Default type | Scale / framing |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| columns | follow brief | Medium scale — self-contained, balanced, even margins. Must read at a glance next to sibling columns. |
| customer_testimonial | photoreal | Full-bleed background. Environmental person-scenario or scenario. Leave a calm negative-space region (keep dead-center clear) for an overlaid quote/name card. Not a tight face close-up. |
| textmedia | follow brief | Flexible — medium to full scale depending on brief and dimensions. |
| testimonial_slider | photoreal, avatar | Head-and-shoulders avatar (image-type-avatar). 512×512. Companion asset if present: product cutout or a small scenario vignette. |

## Lighting

Natural and varied — never default golden-hour treatment:
- Office: cool-neutral morning light
- Cafe: bright window light
- Workshop: soft industrial ambient

Color temperature: 5000–6500K. Clear tonal contrast between subject and background. The aesthetic is bright, natural, and vivid — airy and uplifting. Never flat/uniformly lit. Never dark or moody.

Do not specify camera equipment or brand names in prompts. Let the model draw from its photographic repertoire.

## Color Strategy

- Backgrounds: warm neutrals — cream, sand, light wood, soft white, natural materials
- Props / objects: 2–3 saturated accent colors for visual dynamism — cobalt, terracotta, forest green, mustard, burgundy
- IONOS brand colors (#003D8F, #11C7E6): apply only when the brief explicitly requests them; otherwise let natural object and environment colors drive the palette

## Character Diversity (mandatory — always encode explicitly)

Never leave character demographics undefined. Apply these pools when the brief does not specify.

Encode all chosen characteristics positively in the prompt, early in the prompt (e.g. "a Black woman in her 40s with average build, standing in..."). Never place demographics in negativePrompt.

### Ethnicity pools

Default (no market signal):
- White / Northern-European ~80%
- Black / African descent ~15%
- East or SE Asian ~10%
- South Asian ~5%

Germany / US:
- White / Northern-European ~70%
- Black / African descent ~15%
- East / SE Asian ~10%
- South Asian ~5%

Spain / Italy: Mediterranean / Latin-European ~65% — use "olive complexion and dark hair" not "Latino" or "Hispanic"

France: White/French-European ~55%, North African/Maghrebi ~20%, Black ~15%, East/SE Asian ~10%

### Body shape (role-specific)
- Manual trades: "stocky build" or "solid, muscular build"
- Office work: "average build" or "lean build"

### Age and gender
- Default age: 30s–50s for working adults unless context suggests otherwise
- Gender: vary across image sets; choose based on narrative context

## Environment Storytelling

- Lived-in backgrounds: density and disorder appropriate to each profession. Workshops show works-in-progress and scattered tools; food service shows busy counters; creative studios show reference materials and partial projects.
- Object interaction: characters hold or actively engage with profession-relevant items. This is the strongest authenticity signal — never empty or crossed hands.
- Depth layering (three planes): colorful foreground object as bokeh near lens → sharp subject in middle plane → densely enumerated background elements softly blurred.
- Characters: mid-shift appearance — hair worn effortlessly, functional workwear showing appropriate wear, genuine expressions either engaging the camera or focused on tasks.

## Prompt Construction Order (portrait / person-scenario)

1. Face anchor + camera distance (e.g. "full face clearly visible from hairline to chin, waist-up shot showing complete upper body")
2. Character details (ethnicity, age, body shape, attire)
3. Background density (environment description)
4. Lighting (natural source, color temperature)
5. Natural appearance (mid-shift look, genuine expression)
6. Photography style
7. Foreground bokeh last (only for wider shots)

## Face and Body Framing Rule

Always state framing POSITIVELY in the prompt — never in negativePrompt. Negative prompts are weak composition signals under the model center-crop bias. Use positive instructions:
- "full face visible from hairline to chin, waist-up shot showing complete upper body"
- "full body in frame from head to floor"
- Portrait on landscape ratio: "full face clearly visible from hairline to chin, extra-wide establishing shot, character occupying one vertical third of the frame, full body head to floor visible"

## Standard Negative Prompt Baseline

Always include:
"text, watermark, UI chrome, distorted hands, extra fingers, oversaturated, low quality, jpeg artifacts, readable screen text, readable whiteboard text, legible labels, Apple logo, Nike logo, brand logo, corporate logo, product logo, visible logo, dark moody lighting, flat shadowless lighting, all-grey muted palette"

## Cutout Requirements

- Single clear subject (object, device, person, or motif) centered on a PLAIN, evenly lit, high-contrast background — so the matting model produces a clean alpha edge
- Silhouette must be unambiguous: avoid cluttered backgrounds, subject touching frame borders, or semi-transparent elements such as smoke or glass
- Background removed entirely → transparent PNG
- Aesthetic: cool, premium, understated — aligned with IONOS style

## Aspect Ratio and Crop Safety

Map requested pixel dimensions to nearest standard ratio: 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, 3:2, 9:16, 2:3, 3:4.

Crop safety: the service renders a square then center-crops to the target ratio. Landscape targets trim top/bottom; portrait targets trim left/right — adjust subject positioning to keep key elements in the surviving central band.

- [MUST] Imagery exclusion:
    · Vermeide 3D-Bilder, unrealistische Bildkompositionen, gestellte Szenen/Lachen, gestresst aussehende Personen, alte Hardware, fehlende mobile Endgeräte, zu viel professionelle Hardware, typische Stock-Fotos und sichtbare Markenlogos.
    · Verwenden Sie keine 3D-Bilder von Serverfarmen.
    · Verwenden Sie keine mobilen Geräte; zeigen Sie nur Desktop-PRO-Hardware.
    · Verwenden Sie keine veraltete Hardware (z.B. alter iMac).
    · Vermeiden Sie Menschen, die aussehen, als würden sie sich abmühen.
    · Avoid depicting support staff in a call center environment, and ensure they are captured with a friendly and professional look.
    · Do not use fake or generic happy faces, unrealistic and staged images, clichés, glare, color washes, unfocused images, or unfocused compositions in cluttered environments.
    · Avoid using dark brown tones in photography and videos. (Slightly warmer palettes work for SMBs, but make sure the colors work well with our primary colors.)
    · Ensure visible tattoos or piercings are not apparent on individuals (such as testimonials, personal consultants, or key account managers) when representing the brand in regular campaign activities managed by marketing departments for external communication. (Exceptions apply to influencer content in their regular content, social media content featuring well-known personalities within the context of sponsorship used solely for content production, and employee testimonials as part of HR marketing.)
- [MUST] Imagery composition:
    · Spiegeln Sie die Skalierbarkeit der Hardware in den Bildern wider.
    · Zeigen Sie eine realistische Arbeitsumgebung wie eine Serverfarm/Rechenzentrum oder eine Umgebung mit PRO-Hardware.
    · Berücksichtigen Sie für das Web die Optimierung auf Mobile.
    · For content areas, use on-the-job photography showing natural situations/moments with natural lighting, and do not have the subject look directly into the camera.
    · Keep the background of testimonial photography calm without color fireworks, avoiding farfetched settings, and keeping them looking professional and relatable while including meaningful context.
- [MUST] Imagery casting:
    · Zeigen Sie reflektierende PRO-Anwender-Personas (IT-Entscheider, Agenturen & Entwickler) mit PRO-Hardware.
    · Utilize diverse and realistic portraits (covering ethnicity, age, gender, and body shape) based on data specific to your market.
    · Dress employees in business casual (toned-down colored shirts without a tie, knitwear, or t-shirt & jeans), preferring solid colors and simple designs over patterns, trendy designs, or wrinkles. (Edit the clothing colors to light blue or gray, if needed.)
    · Have employees look directly into the camera with a proud posture, relaxed attitude, and an approachable, friendly look with a natural smile.
    · Ensure testimonials look directly into the camera, assume a proud posture, exude a certain lightness, and display a friendly look with a natural smile.
- [SHOULD] Imagery lighting:
    · Avoid frames that are too colorful or artificial, keep skin tones natural, and make sure the images are vibrant and clear.
    · Use a (semi-)soft focus with a clear portrait and softer background.
    · Whenever possible, use natural lighting while filming or taking photos, or use techniques that simulate natural light unobtrusively.

# IONOS Visual Identity

Source: IONOS Style Guide v2.2

## Color Palette

### Primary Colors (always available)

| Name | Code | HEX | Role |
|------|------|-----|------|
| IONOS Blue | B6 | #003D8F | Logo, primary brand anchor. Frames the brand together with Dark Midnight. |
| Sky | S3 | #11C7E6 | Brand CTA, bold accents. Adds boldness and vibrance — use to direct eyes. One CTA per section maximum. |
| Dark Blue | B7 | #0B2A63 | Background specifically for the white logo. |
| Dark Midnight | B8 | #001B41 | Primary text color for screen — softer than pure black, on-brand. |
| Cloud | C1 | #F4F7FA | Light backgrounds, subtle containers. |
| Blue Black | B9 | #02102B | Base of the basic blue gradient; deep backgrounds. |
| White | — | #FFFFFF | Standard white. |

Print only: Cool Black #0A121C (deeper print black), pure Black #000000 for body text in print.

### Secondary Colors (prior approval required)

Secondary colors require explicit approval. They only work when the surrounding environment already reads as unmistakably IONOS: logo visible, blues dominant at >60% of the color space. Control their proportion and combine with the primary palette.

| Name | Code | HEX | Role |
|------|------|-----|------|
| Amber | Y3 | #FFAA00 | Price badges, illustrations |
| Purple | P4 | #D746F5 | Illustrations; also doubles as the AI gradient magenta end |
| Green | G3 | #12CF76 | Success/status indicators in UI, illustrations |
| Rose | R3 | #FF6159 | Error/value badges, illustrations |

## Color Hierarchy Rules

1. Lead with IONOS Blue and Dark Midnight — these anchor the brand and communicate trust.
2. Sky is directional, not decorative. It should point somewhere: a CTA button, a key statistic, a focal element. One Sky element per section maximum. Overusing it turns a signal into noise.
3. Secondary colors need brand context. The surrounding composition must already feel unmistakably IONOS. If blues are not dominant, drop the secondary color entirely.
4. Cloud and White are backgrounds, not brand colors — they provide breathing room.

## WCAG AA Contrast (pre-approved combinations)

| Combination | Ratio | Status |
|-------------|-------|--------|
| White on Dark Midnight #001B41 | 14.5:1 | Passes AAA |
| Dark Midnight on White | 14.5:1 | Passes AAA |
| Dark Midnight on Cloud #F4F7FA | ~14:1 | Passes AAA |
| White on Dark Blue #0B2A63 | 10.4:1 | Passes AA |
| White on IONOS Blue #003D8F | 4.07:1 | Passes AA for large text only — verify at small sizes |
| Black on Sky #11C7E6 | ~3.5:1 | Passes AA for large text — verify at small sizes |

## Typography

| Typeface | CSS Token | Character | Primary Use |
|----------|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| Overpass | --font-title | Persuasive, guiding, impressive | Headlines (h1–h3), pull quotes, display text |
| Open Sans | --font-base | Informative, reasonable, universal | Body text, UI labels, buttons, navigation |
| Overpass Mono | --font-code | Technical, structured | Code snippets, specifications |

Decision rule:
- Impact / emotion / grabbing attention → Overpass
- Legibility / utility / information → Open Sans (default when unsure)
- Technical / code / specs → Overpass Mono

Rules:
- Overpass weights: Regular (400) and Semibold (600) only — no Bold weight in the brand system
- Open Sans weights: Regular (400), Semibold (600), Bold (700)
- Do not use Overpass below ~20px — legibility degrades at small sizes
- Do not mix Overpass and Open Sans within the same text block
- Small uppercase labels: 0.56px tracking (Figma spec)

## Background Treatment (Illustrations & Animations)

- No technical grid lines. No dot grids, hairlines, blueprint cross-hatches, or engineering-paper textures as background decoration.
- No decorative lines. No sweeping curves, diagonal accent lines, circuit-trace paths, or geometric line-art behind content.
- Solid or gradient only. Use a flat brand color or a two-stop linear/radial gradient between brand hexes (e.g. #003D8F → #001B41, or #02102B → #001B41). A subtle vignette or radial fade is acceptable.
- Content carries the energy. Motion, color, and product detail earn the viewer's attention — not background ornamentation.
- "Technical feel" brief: reach for typography weight, content density, or product-screen detail — NOT grid lines or dot patterns.

## Feature-Highlight Composition (IONOS Pop-Out)

When a brief signals highlight / spotlight / showcase / demonstrate, or describes a user-action → result flow:

- Main frame = the OUTPUT. What the feature produces — the generated result, the deployed page, the finished dashboard. Place center-right. Dense, content-rich. Dark navy surface typical for AI/premium contexts.
- Pop-out = the INPUT / affordance. What the user typed, clicked, dragged, or said. Always the user side of the interaction — never the result. Canonical form: a rounded-pill chat input with typed prompt text.
- Intersection (non-negotiable): the pop-out overlaps the main frame's left (canonical) edge by 25–40% of the pop-out width. A pop-out floating clear is wrong. Fully inside reads as a modal.
- Contrast: light pop-out on dark main frame (white surface, soft drop shadow, no border). Let value contrast do the layering work.
- Pop-out width: ~50–60% of the main frame width. Pop-out height: ~25–40% of main frame height.
- Single pop-out per highlight. Multiple pop-outs dilute focus.
- Animation sequence: pop-out enters first (slide up + fade + scale), main frame materializes second with staggered springs.

## AI Feature Colors

Use ONLY for genuinely AI-driven affordances: prompt inputs, generate/improve-with-AI actions, AI result callouts, AI badges. Never for ordinary CTAs — those stay on brand blue/sky.

Gradient direction: blue → magenta, always 45° static angle. Never animate the gradient angle.

| Token | Hex |
|-------|-----|
| ai-primary-start (blue) | #095BB1 |
| ai-primary-end (magenta) | #D746F5 |
| ai-subtle-start (light) | #FAE7FE |
| ai-subtle-end (light) | #FFFFFF |
| AI accent / semantic-ai | #B410E7 |

Primary AI CTA: `background: linear-gradient(45deg, #095BB1, #D746F5); color: #fff;`
Subtle AI surface (prompt inputs, generating state): `background: linear-gradient(120deg, #FAE7FE, #FFFFFF);`

AI loading state (mandatory): every AI interaction must include a visible generating state between trigger and result. Use ai-subtle as a calm animated background (slow oscillation). Minimum 10–15 frames at 30fps before result reveal. Never cut directly from action to result.

UDS component: `<Button concept="ai" variant="primary">` — variants: primary (full gradient bg + white text), secondary (gradient border + text), tertiary (gradient text only).

## Logo Rules

- Name: IONOS — always all-caps, never "Ionos"
- Clear space: greater than the width of the letter N on all sides
- Minimum size: 3.2mm (print) / 16px (screen)
- Light background: IONOS Blue (#003D8F) logo
- Dark background: white logo on Dark Blue (#0B2A63)
- Nlement: distinctive 26° inclination derived from the N
- Celebrity Backdrop: scaled Nlements protruding from the lower right of the composition
- Forbidden modifications: no drop shadows, no outlines, no transformation or distortion, no complex backgrounds

IONOS

The IONOS communication style is professional, direct, and deeply rooted in technology. It prioritizes clarity and functionality above all else, reflecting a brand that provides the essential digital infrastructure for businesses. The style is minimalist and efficient, stripping away unnecessary fluff to focus on the user's specific goals and the technical reliability of the services provided. Every piece of communication should feel like a tool—useful, precise, and high-quality.

The formality level is high and corporate. IONOS maintains a respectful, professional distance that signals stability and expertise. It does not attempt to be the user's 'friend' but rather their most reliable 'partner'. In English, this means avoiding contractions and casual phrasing. In German-speaking markets, the formal 'Sie' is the absolute standard. It speaks with the weight of an established industry leader rather than the experimental tone of a casual startup.

The tone is authoritative, visionary, and reassuring. It aims to inspire confidence by showcasing its immense scale and technological prowess. The brand voice should make the user feel that their digital presence is in safe, expert hands. By using imagery of vast, connected cityscapes and people looking toward the horizon, the brand positions itself as a guide to the future of digital business, offering a 'big picture' perspective that is both grounded and aspirational.

Be concise and get straight to the point.
Use professional, industry-standard terminology.
Maintain a clean, organized structure in all communications.
Emphasize reliability and global reach.
Use instructional and functional language (e.g., 'Document moved to Brand Portal').

Avoid slang, colloquialisms, or overly informal greetings.
Do not use cluttered or overly complex sentence structures that obscure the main message.
Avoid emotional appeals that feel 'soft' or vague; keep the focus on tangible professional benefits and technical excellence.

Focus on themes of connectivity, digital transformation, and professional empowerment.
Use active, confident verbs that imply progress and stability.

Personality
- Emotionaler Kundennutzen: Einfache Anwendung vermittelt Erfolg und Belohnung. Verlässlichkeit vermittelt Selbstbewusstsein und Motivation. Sicherheit vermittelt Ruhe und Gewissheit. Service vermittelt Vertrauen, Unterstützung und Partnerschaftlichkeit.
- Brand Perception Values: Verlässlichkeit, Glaubwürdigkeit, Zusammenarbeit, Effizienz, Unternehmenswachstum, Unterstützung, Verantwortung, Professionalität, Selbständigkeit.

Brand image
- Gefühl von Kontrolle: Kunden, die kein Vertrauen in Agenturen oder kein Budget haben, erhalten eine sichere, einfache SEO-Strategie, die das Risiko zu scheitern minimiert. Dies vermittelt ein Gefühl von Kontrolle – Kunden behalten den Überblick und sparen Geld.
- Empowerment und Erfolg: Kunden, die bei Google gut gefunden werden wollen, erhalten durch rankingCoach leicht umzusetzende Lösungsschritte. Dies führt zu einem Gefühl von Empowerment und Erfolg – Kunden können sich selbst um ihr SEO kümmern.
- Emotionen und Wahrnehmung: Zuverlässigkeit, Glaubwürdigkeit, Partnerschaft, Effizienz, Support, Zugehörigkeitsgefühl, Professionalität, Autonomie, Unabhängigkeit, Sicherheit
- Emotionen und Wahrnehmung: Indem wir ein Gefühl beim Kunden hervorrufen, bewegen wir ihn zum Kauf. Gehe auf seine Bedürfnisse ein, ohne aufdringlich oder unglaubwürdig zu werden. Biete dem Kunden Lösungen. Relevante Faktoren sind: Preis, Marken-Reputation, Einfach zu transferieren, Features, Angebot, Mengenrabatte, Performance/Leistung, Sicherheit, Schnelle Problemlösungen, Kundenservice, Einfache Anwendung.

Mission (Brand, global): To be the European Cloud Platform for digital success – by providing businesses with robust infrastructure, expert guidance and solutions that grow with their needs.
Cloud Platform Positioning: From easy to use DIY with state-of-the-art tech in the background, to the expertise and resources of creating custom solutions at enterprise scale, the IONOS Cloud Platform helps customers operate and grow their businesses.
Hero Archetype Definition: IONOS uses the hero archetype, whose traits are reflected by the brand's character. Because when we see ourselves –and our customers– as heroes, we can tell stories that stick in people’s minds.
Prometheus Hero Story Guidance: As guidance, we can use the heroic saga of Prometheus, who took the fire from the gods of Olympus to give it to mankind so that it could become independent. In this independence, the self-image of our customers is mirrored by our European Cloud Platform: To set a sustainable, confident counterpoint to 'the big guys up there'.
Hero Story: Being able to tell a compelling story enables us to break out of the "rational sameness" of our industry. As guidance, we use the heroic saga of Prometheus, who took the fire from the gods of Olympus to give it to mankind so that it could become independent. In this independence, the self-image of our customers is mirrored by our European Cloud Platform: to set a sustainable, confident counterpoint to "the big guys up there". We do not hide our European origin — the virtues associated with it, such as social market economy, sustainability and data protection, are further great arguments to identify with the IONOS brand.
Tonalität: Selbstbewusst und einnehmend, Freundlich und hilfsbereit, Ermutigend und inspirierend.
Personality: Confident: We’re proud of the value we provide
Confident: We're proud of the value we provide.

Because we’re secure in our own value as a brand, we keep it positive and don’t need to resort to fear-based marketing. By being confident, we inspire confidence in our audience. We are approachable — never overbearing or arrogant. We make sure our content is accessible and engaging.
Personality: Dedicated: We act with intention and focus on facts.
Dedicated: We act with intention and focus on facts.

Support is a key value proposition, so we tie this when it makes sense to do so. We are thorough and give our audience the information they need, without being patronising. However, concise is always better than long-winded — everything we write should be relevant.
Personality: Ambitious: We are driven and strive to inspire others.
Ambitious: We are driven and strive to inspire others.
Tone: Encouraging and Inspirational: We are ambitious for ourselves, and for others. We want to grow as a company, and help our customers grow with us. We understand that not everyone has the same time, skills or goals, so we keep our messaging inclusive, or tailor it to particular audiences where appropriate.
